Tosafot on Bava Batra 69b:3:1.hebrew: ארעא ודיקלי אי אית בה דיקלי כו' - אע"ג דאם לא אמר דיקלי בסתמא היו כולן מכורין, מיהו השתא גרע, כדבעי למימר לקמן: חוץ מחרוב פלוני, דקני שאר חרובין, אע"ג דבסתמא לא קני, דדיקלי משמע תרי. ולא שייך הכא "שופרא דשטרא", אלא דוקא כשכותב בשטר; אבל הכא דבעל פה — לא. ועוד, דהתם כתיב "דיקלין ותאלין כו'", והכא דלא קאמר אלא "דיקלין" — לא שייך למימר הכי:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 69b:3:1.english: "Land and date palms" – if there are date palms in it, etc. - Even though, had he not said "date palms" at all, they would all have been sold [along with the land], nevertheless now it is worse [for the buyer], as [the Gemara] is about to say later: [if the seller said,] "except for such-and-such carob tree," the buyer acquires [only] the other carob trees, even though without [that statement] he would not have acquired them, since "dikelei" implies two [at least]. And the concept of "the beauty of the document" (shufra de-shetara) does not apply here, but only when he writes it in a document; but here, where [the sale] is oral — it does not [apply]. Furthermore, there [in the earlier case] it is written "dikelin and te'alin, etc.," whereas here, where he said only "dikelin," it is not possible to say this.
